chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Rayyan, from Ali ibn Muhammad, known as Ibn Wahba al-Abdasi, and it is a town from the towns of Wasit, raising it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The best of the stones (for rings) is the crystal.

key_terms.بِلَّوْرُ: Crystal or rock crystal, a clear gemstone.
key_terms.فَصُّ: The setting or stone set in a ring.

ai.seo_question: What is the best type of stone for a ring according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the term 'bawlur' (crystal) is praised as the finest material for rings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on simplicity and purity in adornment. This hadith is situated within the broader jurisprudential discourse on *takhalluq* (adornment), where clear stones are preferred to avoid the ostentation associated with precious gems like emeralds or rubies. It underscores the principle that permissible luxury should remain modest, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of wearing simple silver or clear stone rings.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Rayyan, from Ali Bin Muhammad well known as Ibn Wahba Al Abdasy, and it is a town from the towns of Wasit,
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said, The best of the stones (for rings) is the crystal’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Rayyan from Ali ibn Muhammad known as ibn Wahbah al-‘Abdasiy which is a town in Wasit in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
‘Al-Billur (crystal) is very good for the stone of a ring.”’
